versions.kind: 同文消息 · 最早检出的版本
versions.note: 原版为 dismasted；RevX 的 distressed 是转写差异。扫描中船长姓名字形与 RevX 的 Boye 也不宜用于人物去重。此处未附后见版本的 CHRONICLE 质疑。
versions.excerpt: Captain Boye positively asserts, that previous to his failing, accounts were received at the custom-house of Liverpool, of 17 sail of French vessels, men of war and transports, having a number of troops on board, destined for a descent on Ireland, being through gusts of weather blown into Bantry Bay, most of them distressed; some of the people went on shore, were made prisoners, and sent to Dublin; from the situation of the place the whole must inevitably be captured. They intended to have effected a landing at Londonderry in the North of Ireland.

versions.kind: 同文消息 + 署名 CHRONICLE 的质疑
versions.note: 质疑同时提出日期、路线与人数问题；它也是当时人的解释，不能自动充当事实核查结果。RevX 的 failed 在此为原报 sailed。
versions.excerpt: Capt. Boyd, positively asserts, that previous to his sailing, accounts were received at the custom house of Liverpool, of 17 sail of French vessels, men of war and transports, having a number of troops on board, destined for a DESCENT ON IRELAND, being through stress of weather, blown into Bantry Bay, most of them dismasted; some of the people went on shore, were made prisoners, and went to Dublin; from the situation of the place the whole must inevitably be captured. They intended to have effected a landing at Londonderry in the North of Ireland. [NOTE. Capt. Boyd failed from Liverpool on the 29th December, and the French fleet left Brest, on the 26th of the same month: How then is it possible they should have reached Ireland in 3 days, and the accounts from thence received at Liverpool? Can it be thought that 20,000 French troops, and 17 ships of the line, have surrendered to the inhabitants of Bantry, whose population does not exceed 10,000 souls? It is more natural to think the French have taken that town.—Why were those 20,000 French sent to Dublin, 154 miles from Bantry Bay, and not to Cork, that lies but 9 miles from it? Can it be presumed, that the French fleet, in order to effect a landing at Londonderry, had entered the channel of Ireland so full of dangers, instead of sailing westward, on the main; a route much shorter and less difficult, free from the dangers of the channel, and which would not have exposed them to discovery from Liverpool or Dublin, and meet with every obstacle, that could have frustrated their design. CHRONICLE.]

versions.kind: 后续综述 · 另一种结局
versions.note: 同一报纸七天后刊出综述，称舰队已分批返回 Brest。未明确点名撤回此前 Boyd 消息，因此不标成正式更正。
versions.excerpt: Of the intelligence brought by the late arrivals, the most important relates to the French expedition against Ireland. We have collected under this head, every interesting detail we have been able to meet with. By comparing the various accounts, it appears, that the French force when it failed from Brest, consisted of about 50 sail, including transports, of which 17 were of the line, and had on board 25,000 men.—They failed in three divisions, under the command of De Galles, Bouvet and Neuilly; the land troops under the command of general Hoche. They had scarcely left the port when bad weather dispersed them. Chief part of the fleet however rendezvoused at Bantry Bay, but the frigate la Fraternite, on board of which were the commanders of the fleet and land forces, not joining the fleet, after some delay left the Bay, without molestation, except by the wind, and by the best and latest accounts, reached Brest, in divisions without material loss. The expedition appears to have been planned on a large scale. The Toulon fleet which came round to l'Orient, and the armament at Dunkirk were probably to co-operate. Notwithstanding the above failure, the French appear still to have an expedition to Ireland in contemplation.

Allen was from Dover, bound for Surinam, but touched at Cayenne, where he had been several days before the seizure was made. The pretext was, his being from an English port.

versions.kind: 卡宴法令译文 + 编辑指控
versions.note: 后附评论称所引事例八条中七条虚假，却未在该处逐条列证。记录为“失实指控”，不录入已证实的假新闻数；原始卡宴报和被引八条消息仍缺失。
versions.excerpt: It is easy to perceive, that the American papers, cited in this decree, are the Jacobin Gazettes of the United States, and that the instances quoted, are seven out of eight, false and scandalous. It is also very evident, that the French Agents, in the United States, have published those very accounts in the Aurora , Argus , Chronicle , and other hiring papers, merely to give a pretext to the plunderers in the West-Indies, to seize and confiscate American vessels, and that the Printers of them have been base and sordid enough to send them those papers, in order that they may be adduced as documents, to justify their infamy! The American merchants and seamen, who suffer under the piracies in the West-Indies, now look to those Printers as the Authors of their misery; and were they to prosecute for reparation, an honest jury would do no less than grant a verdict in their favor.

versions.excerpt: On the 7th inst. it was Resolved, by Congress, That the President of the U. S. be authorized to direct clearances to be granted to any ship or vessel, belonging to citizens of the U. S. which are now loaded, bound from any port in the U. S. for any port beyond the Cape of Good Hope; any thing in the resolution for laying the embargo, to the contrary notwithstanding: Provided, That before the collector of either of the districts of the U. S. shall grant clearances, or any such vessel shall sail, the owners thereof shall give sufficient security to the satisfaction of such collector, that she shall not unload her cargo, or any part thereof, at any port or place previous to her arrival at the Cape of Good Hope.

versions.kind: 放行决议 · 带批准日期的版本
versions.note: 包括 May 7, 1794 与 Washington 批准信息。已与《Statutes at Large》第1卷第401页决议 V 对照；核对的是条文，不是执行成效。
versions.excerpt: The following Resolution passed both Houses, and was signed by the President this day.— Resolved, That the President of the United States be authorized to direct clearances to be granted to any ship or vessel, belonging to citizens of the United States, which are now loaded, bound from any port in the United States, for any port beyond the Cape of Good Hope; any thing in the resolution for laying the Embargo, to the contrary notwithstanding: Provided , That before the Collector of either of the districts of the United States, shall grant clearances, or any such vessel shall sail, the owners thereof shall give sufficient security to the satisfaction of such collector, that she shall not unlade her cargo, or any part thereof, at any port or place, previous to her arrival at the Cape of Good Hope. Approved, May 7, 1794. GEO. WASHINGTON, President of the United States.
